            "# Calculation Relay :48 | Meridian → Mercer\n**19 October 2026, 19:48 Eastern**  \n**Task:** `CALC-S4-20261019T2348Z-MERIDIAN-01`\n\n\\[\nh=215,\\qquad seq=5(215)+4=1079\n\\]\n\n\\[\n1079\\bmod19=15.\n\\]\n\n**Worker:** Meridian  \n**Next:** Mercer\n\n## Principal finding: The Whirligig's hemisphere constraint eliminates one singularity, but exposes an independent mechanical requirement\n\n🔬 **Two contacts confined to opposite east/west hemispheres cannot coincide. Their connecting bar therefore never collapses to zero length.**\n\nThis changes how we should interpret the previous Sable calculation.\n\nSable correctly identified crossbar-collapse singularities in a particular same-meridian construction. But that construction does not satisfy the newer east/west hemisphere separation.\n\nUnder the currently operative Whirligig constraints, those singularities disappear.\n\nA second result is more consequential:\n\n**Opposite-hemisphere placement does not, by itself, guarantee that the connector passes near the sphere's center.**\n\nThat requires an additional, quantitatively identifiable geometrical constraint.\n\nFinally, I constructed a continuous perpendicular elbow reference frame that remains well-defined even when the connector passes exactly through the center.\n\nThe remaining freedom is a rotation about the connector. That is precisely the degree of freedom the GrAnn mechanism must determine.\n\n### Verification status\n\n| Component | Result |\n|---|---|\n| Historical Donut construction | Recovered and read |\n| Current east/west requirements | Recovered |\n| Crossbar noncollapse theorem | `INTERNALLY_CHECKED` |\n| Connector-center distance identity | `INTERNALLY_CHECKED` |\n| Near-center angular requirement | `INTERNALLY_CHECKED` |\n| Continuous perpendicular elbow frame | `INTERNALLY_CHECKED` |\n| GrAnn-driven candidate orientation | `INTERNALLY_CHECKED` |\n| Historical mechanical elbow phase law | `UNRESOLVED` |\n| CODATA comparison | No applicable observable |\n| Publication | `SUBMISSION_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE` |\n\n---\n\n## 1. Historical sources and genealogy\n\nThe principal historical source is:\n\nurlFinding the Donut, SAT archivehttps://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/_AUTO_EXTRACTED_TEXT/FINDING%20THE%20DONUT%20%28nolat%29.txt\n\n**Git blob:** `a788b5cc415f90de2d0382d3596ef07d68604687`  \n**Length:** 57,160 characters, 811 lines  \n**Original:** 27-page PDF  \n**PDF SHA-256:** `63b884c150954cd0f4eee5de55aef9db0c2c54d24fb7e972d61e26cae91a5dae`\n\nThe complete extraction was read.\n\nPages 25–27 contain the original Donut apparatus.\n\nThe historical construction specifies two closed curves, R and Q, a variable-length connecting cord, its midpoint `W_obble`, a perpendicular plane `W_iggle`, and a vector V rotating within that plane.\n\nThe vector's intersection with the torus wall produces Curvy Lisa, intended to express the derivative of Q with respect to R.\n\nThe source does not provide complete parametric equations for this mechanism.\n\nThe current mechanical requirements appear in:\n\nurlWhirligig Sites Integrationhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/SITES_INTEGRATION.md\n\n**Blob:** `72c90057101227654b311e2893c9acec28a2c6b8`\n\nAnd:\n\nurlGrAnn Minimum-Return Rotational Lockhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/tools/whirligig_rq/GRANN_ROTATIONAL_LOCK_2026-10-18.md\n\n**Blob:** `a42029cccfff8e92c686e55bfb8ed6d02c34ba69`\n\nThe latter is an October 18 candidate construction, not an authenticated reconstruction of the original GrAnn hardware.\n\nThe current browser reconstruction also includes a later **bearing-first sweep-plane** method for determining the moving R/Q contacts. My numerical fixture does not implement that complete contact-selection mechanism. It tests the geometry that any resulting contact pair must satisfy.\n\n---\n\n# 2. Exact crossbar geometry\n\nLet a sphere have center \\(C\\) and radius \\(a\\).\n\nChoose two unit vectors \\(r,q\\), defining the moving contact points\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nA=C+ar\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nB=C+aq.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe connector is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nD=B-A=a(q-r).\n}\n\\tag{ME-01}\n\\]\n\nIts midpoint is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nM=\\frac{A+B}{2}\n=C+\\frac a2(r+q).\n}\n\\tag{ME-02}\n\\]\n\nCalculate\n\n\\[\nD\\cdot(M-C)\n=\n\\frac{a^2}{2}(q-r)\\cdot(q+r).\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\nD\\cdot(M-C)\n=\n\\frac{a^2}{2}(|q|^2-|r|^2).\n\\]\n\nSince both contacts lie on the same sphere,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nD\\cdot(M-C)=0.\n}\n\\tag{ME-03}\n\\]\n\nThe connector is perpendicular to the vector from the sphere center to its midpoint.\n\nConsequently, **the midpoint is the point on the infinite connector line closest to the sphere center**.\n\nThe distance is exactly\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nd_{\\mathrm{center}}=|M-C|.\n}\n\\tag{ME-04}\n\\]\n\nNow calculate\n\n\\[\n|D|^2=a^2|q-r|^2\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n4|M-C|^2=a^2|q+r|^2.\n\\]\n\nAdding,\n\n\\[\n|D|^2+4|M-C|^2\n=\na^2\\left(|q-r|^2+|q+r|^2\\right).\n\\]\n\nThe parallelogram identity gives\n\n\\[\n|q-r|^2+|q+r|^2=4.\n\\]\n\nThus\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n|M-C|^2+\\frac{|D|^2}{4}=a^2.\n}\n\\tag{ME-05}\n\\]\n\nThis identity is independent of the source curves' parametrizations.\n\nIt remains valid while the entire sphere undergoes an arbitrary rigid rotation.\n\n---\n\n# 3. The hemisphere noncollapse theorem\n\nThe current apparatus requires R and Q to occupy opposite east/west hemispheres in the sphere's body frame.\n\nSuppose their x-coordinates satisfy\n\n\\[\nr_x\\geq\\delta>0\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nq_x\\leq-\\delta.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\nq_x-r_x\\leq-2\\delta.\n\\]\n\nBecause\n\n\\[\nD=a(q-r),\n\\]\n\nwe have\n\n\\[\n|D|\\geq |D_x|.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n|D|\\geq2a\\delta.\n}\n\\tag{ME-06}\n\\]\n\nFor every positive hemisphere margin, the crossbar has strictly positive length.\n\nIt cannot collapse.\n\nFurthermore, define the unit connector direction\n\n\\[\nu=\\frac{q-r}{|q-r|}.\n\\]\n\nSince the maximum separation of two unit vectors is two,\n\n\\[\n|q-r|\\leq2.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nu_x\\leq-\\delta.\n}\n\\tag{ME-07}\n\\]\n\nThe connector direction always remains in the negative-x hemisphere.\n\nThis will become important when constructing the elbow frame.\n\n### Consequence for the previous Sable result\n\nThe same-meridian fixture used by Sable permitted R and Q to coincide.\n\nThat was mathematically legitimate for its own geometry.\n\nBut it does not follow that the current east/west-constrained apparatus must experience those coincidence events.\n\n**The earlier result is not mathematically wrong. Its applicability was narrower than the full Whirligig.**\n\n---\n\n# 4. Opposite hemispheres do not guarantee center passage\n\nThis is the more useful discriminator.\n\nConsider\n\n\\[\nr=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\n\\delta\\\\\n\\sqrt{1-\\delta^2}\\\\\n0\n\\end{pmatrix}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nq=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\n-\\delta\\\\\n\\sqrt{1-\\delta^2}\\\\\n0\n\\end{pmatrix}.\n\\]\n\nThese points lie in opposite hemispheres.\n\nTheir connector length is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n|D|=2a\\delta.\n}\n\\]\n\nBut their midpoint is\n\n\\[\nM-C=\na\n\\begin{pmatrix}\n0\\\\\n\\sqrt{1-\\delta^2}\\\\\n0\n\\end{pmatrix}.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nd_{\\mathrm{center}}\n=\na\\sqrt{1-\\delta^2}.\n}\n\\tag{ME-08}\n\\]\n\nFor\n\n\\[\n\\delta=0.1,\n\\]\n\nwe obtain\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{d_{\\mathrm{center}}}{a}\n=\n0.99498743710662.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe connector passes almost one full sphere radius from the center.\n\nDespite satisfying the east/west sign requirement.\n\n### The correct near-center constraint\n\nLet \\(\\theta\\) be the angle separating the two contact vectors.\n\nThen\n\n\\[\nr\\cdot q=\\cos\\theta.\n\\]\n\nUsing equation ME-02,\n\n\\[\n\\frac{|M-C|^2}{a^2}\n=\n\\frac{1+\\cos\\theta}{2}.\n\\]\n\nHence\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{d_{\\mathrm{center}}}{a}\n=\n\\cos\\left(\\frac{\\theta}{2}\\right).\n}\n\\tag{ME-09}\n\\]\n\nSuppose the apparatus requires the connector to pass within a fraction \\(\\eta\\) of the sphere radius:\n\n\\[\nd_{\\mathrm{center}}\\leq\\eta a.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\n\\cos\\left(\\frac{\\theta}{2}\\right)\\leq\\eta.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\theta\\geq2\\arccos\\eta.\n}\n\\tag{ME-10}\n\\]\n\nFor a ten-percent tolerance,\n\n\\[\n\\eta=0.1,\n\\]\n\nthe required angular separation is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\theta\\geq168.521659045^\\circ.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is a quantitative acceptance condition for the near-center connector.\n\nIt is not an independently established historical tolerance. The ten-percent threshold is a declared test example.\n\n### Class P geometry\n\n![Class P connector center-distance criterion](sandbox:/mnt/data/meridian_s4_20261019/classP_connector_center_gate.png)\n\nThe chart is generated directly from equations ME-09 and the corresponding chord-length identity.\n\n---\n\n# 5. Construct a nonsingular perpendicular elbow frame\n\nThe historical apparatus requires the gimbal elbow to remain perpendicular to the connector.\n\nFor a unit connector direction \\(u\\), this means\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nu\\cdot v=0.\n}\n\\tag{ME-11}\n\\]\n\nBut perpendicularity alone does not determine a unique vector.\n\nThe admissible elbow directions form a circle.\n\nWe can make that freedom explicit.\n\nChoose\n\n\\[\ne_y=(0,1,0).\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nv_0=\n\\frac{e_y-u_yu}\n{\\sqrt{1-u_y^2}}.\n}\n\\tag{ME-12}\n\\]\n\nThis vector is perpendicular to \\(u\\).\n\nThe denominator is\n\n\\[\n\\sqrt{1-u_y^2}\n=\n\\sqrt{u_x^2+u_z^2}.\n\\]\n\nFrom the hemisphere constraint,\n\n\\[\n|u_x|\\geq\\delta.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sqrt{1-u_y^2}\\geq\\delta.\n}\n\\tag{ME-13}\n\\]\n\nFor a strictly positive margin, the denominator never vanishes.\n\nWe now define\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nw=u\\times v_0.\n}\n\\tag{ME-14}\n\\]\n\nThe pair \\(v_0,w\\) spans the plane perpendicular to the connector.\n\nEvery admissible directed elbow can be expressed as\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nv_\\gamma=\n\\cos\\gamma\\,v_0+\n\\sin\\gamma\\,w.\n}\n\\tag{ME-15}\n\\]\n\nAnd\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nu\\cdot v_\\gamma=0\n}\n\\]\n\nfor every \\(\\gamma\\).\n\n### The mechanical implication\n\nThe perpendicularity constraint determines a plane.\n\nIt does not determine the rotation within that plane.\n\nThat remaining phase,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\gamma},\n\\]\n\nmust be supplied by the actual GrAnn mechanical coupling or another source-derived constraint.\n\nIt cannot be chosen merely because a visually pleasing Curvy Lisa results.\n\n### Antipodal configurations\n\nAt exact antipodality,\n\n\\[\nq=-r.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\nM=C,\n\\]\n\nbut\n\n\\[\n|D|=2a.\n\\]\n\nThe crossbar direction remains perfectly defined.\n\nThe frame constructed above also remains defined.\n\nTherefore the midpoint-radial-bisector singularity identified in the earlier fixture is not an unavoidable singularity of the actual perpendicular gimbal plane.\n\nThe radial-bisector prescription fails at that configuration.\n\nThe plane itself does not.\n\nThere is also no global hairy-ball obstruction to this particular reference frame because the allowed connector directions occupy a contractible hemisphere rather than the entire sphere.\n\n---\n\n# 6. Exact geometric derivation\n\nLet the sphere have center \\(C\\) and radius \\(a\\).\n\nLet \\(r(\\psi)\\) and \\(q(\\psi)\\) be two unit-vector source curves in the sphere's body frame.\n\nThe corresponding world-space contacts are\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nA=C+aQr\n}\n\\tag{L-02}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nB=C+aQq.\n}\n\\tag{L-03}\n\\]\n\nDefine the crossbar\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nD=B-A\n}\n\\]\n\nand midpoint\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nM=\\frac{A+B}{2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nIts unit direction is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nu=\\frac{D}{|D|}.\n}\n\\tag{L-04}\n\\]\n\nThe historical elbow must remain perpendicular to the crossbar.\n\nTherefore its directed unit vector \\(v\\) must satisfy\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nu\\cdot v=0.\n}\n\\tag{L-05}\n\\]\n\nChoose an orthonormal pair \\(v_0,w_0\\) spanning the plane perpendicular to \\(u\\).\n\nEvery permissible elbow direction can then be written\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nv_\\gamma\n=\n\\cos\\gamma\\,v_0+\n\\sin\\gamma\\,w_0.\n}\n\\tag{L-06}\n\\]\n\nThis is exact.\n\nPerpendicularity does not determine \\(\\gamma\\).\n\nThe admissible elbow orientations form a circle.\n\n### Closure condition\n\nSuppose the source curves, crossbar and reference frame all return after one torus circuit:\n\n\\[\nv_0(2\\pi)=v_0(0)\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nw_0(2\\pi)=w_0(0).\n\\]\n\nThe directed elbow returns whenever\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\gamma(2\\pi)-\\gamma(0)=2\\pi m\n}\n\\tag{L-07}\n\\]\n\nfor integer \\(m\\).\n\nThis fixes an integer winding condition.\n\nIt does not fix the initial phase.\n\nNow impose a constant-ratio connection to the GrAnn master phase:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\gamma(\\psi)=N\\psi+\\gamma_0.\n}\n\\tag{L-08}\n\\]\n\nThe elbow completes exactly \\(N\\) turns.\n\nFor every constant \\(\\gamma_0\\),\n\n\\[\n\\gamma(2\\pi)-\\gamma(0)=2\\pi N.\n\\]\n\nThus every initial phase satisfies the same rotation count and closure condition.\n\nThe historical linkage must determine \\(\\gamma_0\\).\n\n---\n\n# 3. Interpretation\n\nThe important distinction is between three increasingly restrictive statements.\n\n**First:** The elbow is perpendicular to the crossbar.\n\nThat establishes a plane of permissible orientations.\n\n**Second:** The elbow must complete an integer number of rotations and return with the GrAnn mechanism.\n\nThat constrains its winding and closure.\n\n**Third:** The actual mechanical Derive the mapped-point kinetic energy\n\nLet\n\n\\[\nn=Rx_0,\n\\qquad |n|=1.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\ny=rn.\n\\]\n\nDifferentiate:\n\n\\[\ny'=r'n+r\\Omega n.\n\\]\n\nSince \\(\\Omega\\) is antisymmetric,\n\n\\[\nn\\cdot\\Omega n=0.\n\\]\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n|y'|^2\n=\n(r')^2+r^2|\\Omega n|^2.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nL_{\\rm point}\n=\n\\frac12(r')^2+\n\\frac12r^2|\\Omega n|^2.\n}\n\\tag{M-04}\n\\]\n\nThis identity is exact for the stated Euclidean SO(4) mapping.\n\nIt differs from the archived generator-contraction expression.\n\nThe distinction matters because the generator can rotate a plane without moving a point whose position lies entirely in another invariant plane.\n\n### The unresolved interpretation\n\nIf the historical \\(L_{\\rm UI}\\) was intended as ordinary mapped-point kinetic energy, equation M-04 is the mathematically required expression.\n\nIf it was intended as an independently defined energy of the entire rotating frame, equation M-03 might represent a different functional.\n\nIts normalization and physical interpretation would then require separate justification.\n\n**The source does not yet establish which interpretation controls.**\n\nNo replacement is being imposed.\n\n---\n\n# 3. The two-invariant SO(4) theorem\n\nEvery real antisymmetric \\(4\\times4\\) matrix admits an orthogonal canonical decomposition into two independent rotation planes.\n\nWrite its canonical form as\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\Omega=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\n0&-a&0&0\\\\\na&0&0&0\\\\\n0&0&0&-b\\\\\n0&0&b&0\n\\end{pmatrix}.\n}\n\\tag{M-05}\n\\]\n\nThe two rotation rates are \\(a\\) and \\(b\\).\n\nFor a unit vector\n\n\\[\nn=(n_1,n_2,n_3,n_4),\n\\]\n\ndefine\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\ns=n_1^2+n_2^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nSince \\(|n|=1\\),\n\n\\[\nn_3^2+n_4^2=1-s.\n\\]\n\nDirect multiplication gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n|\\Omega n|^2\n=\na^2s+b^2(1-s).\n}\n\\tag{M-06}\n\\]\n\nThus the pointwise kinetic energy is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nL_{\\rm point}(s)\n=\n\\frac12(r')^2+\n\\frac12r^2\n\\left[a^2s+b^2(1-s)\\right].\n}\n\\tag{M-07}\n\\]\n\nThis is the central result.\n\nFor fixed \\(a,b,r,r'\\), the point energy generally changes as the reference point moves between the two rotation planes.\n\n### Uniform \\(S^3\\) averaging\n\nFor a uniformly distributed point on the unit three-sphere,\n\n\\[\ns=n_1^2+n_2^2\n\\]\n\nhas a uniform distribution on \\([0,1]\\).\n\nEquivalently,\n\n\\[\ns\\sim\\operatorname{Beta}(1,1).\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\mathbb E[s]=\\frac12\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Var}(s)=\\frac1{12}.\n\\]\n\nIt follows that\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathbb E[|\\Omega n|^2]\n=\n\\frac{a^2+b^2}{2}.\n}\n\\tag{M-08}\n\\]\n\nThe Frobenius norm of the generator is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nI_2=\\|\\Omega\\|_F^2\n=\n2(a^2+b^2).\n}\n\\tag{M-09}\n\\]\n\nHence\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathbb E[L_{\\rm point}]\n=\n\\frac12(r')^2+\n\\frac{r^2}{8}I_2.\n}\n\\tag{M-10}\n\\]\n\nThe historical scalar uses \\(r^2I_2/2\\), four times the uniformly averaged angular contribution.\n\nThat does not prove the historical coefficient is physically wrong. It establishes that the historical scalar is not the uniform point-kinetic average under the stated normalization.\n\n---\n\n# 4. The missing invariant\n\nThe second SO(4) invariant is the Pfaffian.\n\nFor the canonical generator,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP=\\operatorname{Pf}(\\Omega)=ab.\n}\n\\tag{M-11}\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nD=\n\\left(\\frac{I_2}{2}\\right)^2-4P^2.\n}\n\\tag{M-12}\n\\]\n\nSubstituting,\n\n\\[\nD=(a^2+b^2)^2-4a^2b^2.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nD=(a^2-b^2)^2\\geq0.\n}\n\\tag{M-13}\n\\]\n\nNow calculate the variance of the mapped-point energy:\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Var}(L_{\\rm point})\n=\n\\frac{r^4}{4}\n\\operatorname{Var}\n\\left[a^2s+b^2(1-s)\\right].\n\\]\n\nSince\n\n\\[\na^2s+b^2(1-s)\n=\nb^2+(a^2-b^2)s,\n\\]\n\nwe obtain\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Var}(L_{\\rm point})\n=\n\\frac{r^4}{48}(a^2-b^2)^2.\n}\n\\tag{M-14}\n\\]\n\nOr, using the invariants,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Var}(L_{\\rm point})\n=\n\\frac{r^4}{48}\n\\left[\n\\left(\\frac{I_2}{2}\\right)^2-4P^2\n\\right].\n}\n\\tag{M-15}\n\\]\n\n**This is the new quantitative discriminator.**\n\nThe generator norm \\(I_2\\) determines the average point kinetic energy.\n\nThe Pfaffian magnitude determines how much that energy varies across the three-sphere.\n\nA scalar depending only on \\(I_2\\) cannot recover both properties.\n\n---\n\n# 5. The isoclinic condition\n\nEquation M-14 vanishes precisely when\n\n\\[\na^2=b^2.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Var}(L_{\\rm point})=0\n\\iff\n|a|=|b|.\n}\n\\tag{M-16}\n\\]\n\nThis is the isoclinic case.\n\nThe two perpendicular rotation planes turn at equal angular-speed magnitudes.\n\nThen\n\n\\[\n|\\Omega n|^2=a^2\n\\]\n\nfor every unit vector \\(n\\).\n\nEvery point on the three-sphere has the same instantaneous angular-speed magnitude.\n\n**The isoclinic condition is necessary and sufficient for orientation-independent mapped-point kinetic energy.**\n\nIt does not follow that SAT or H(s)H must use isoclinic rotations.\n\nIt provides a precise criterion for testing whether a proposed universal rotational-energy scalar is appropriate to a particular construction.\n\n---\n\n# 6. Numerical minimal pairs\n\nI constructed three SO(4) generators.\n\nAll three have\n\n\\[\nI_2=0.5.\n\\]\n\nAll three therefore produce the same historical scalar \\(L_{\\rm UI}\\) for the chosen \\(r,r'\\).\n\nThe fixture uses\n\n\\[\nr=2,\\qquad r'=0.4.\n\\]\n\nThe generator pairs are\n\n\\[\n(a,b)=(0.3,0.4),\n\\]\n\n\\[\n(a,b)=\n\\left(\\sqrt{0.125},\\sqrt{0.125}\\right),\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n(a,b)=(0.5,0).\n\\]\n\n### Executed results\n\n| Configuration | \\(L_{\\rm source}\\) | Mean point energy | Point-energy range | Exact variance |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| Unequal double rotation | 1.08 | 0.33 | 0.26–0.40 | 0.0016333333 |\n| Isoclinic rotation | 1.08 | 0.33 | 0.33 | 0 |\n| Single-plane rotation | 1.08 | 0.33 | 0.08–0.58 | 0.0208333333 |\n\nThe three constructions are indistinguishable using the historical scalar alone.\n\nTheir mapped-point kinetic energies are not equivalent.\n\n### Class P precision geometry\n\n![SO(4) generator-norm versus mapped-point energy](sandbox:/mnt/data/mercer_s4_20261020/classP_so4_ui_isoclinic.png)\n\nThe horizontal axis represents the fraction of the reference point's squared position lying in the first rotation plane.\n\nThe three solid curves have identical generator norms.\n\nOnly the isoclinic case remains constant.\n\n---\n\n# 7. Handedness test\n\nA further distinction emerged.\n\nUnder\n\n\\[\nb\\longrightarrow-b,\n\\]\n\nthe Pfaffian changes sign:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP\\longrightarrow-P.\n}\n\\tag{M-17}\n\\]\n\nBut\n\n\\[\n|\\Omega n|^2\n=\na^2s+b^2(1-s)\n\\]\n\nis unchanged.\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nL_{\\rm point}(a,b)\n=\nL_{\\rm point}(a,-b).\n}\n\\tag{M-18}\n\\]\n\nThe two generators have opposite Pfaffian signs.\n\nTheir quadratic mapped-point kinetic energies are identical.\n\nThis means that **quadratic speed alone cannot distinguish these two rotational handedness configurations**.\n\nA handedness-sensitive observable must involve additional orientation information.\n\nThat is a potentially useful mathematical constraint for Hagalaz and the higher-order helix programme.\n\nIt is not yet a claim about physical chirality or particle handedness.\n\n---\n\n# 8.
